item.title: Did the British Museum Remove Palestine From Its Displays?
item.description: The institution acknowledged altering some texts to refer to Canaan, an ancient name for the region, but said the word “Palestine” still appears elsewhere.

item.title: Lunar New Year-Ramadan Resolutions
item.description: The British Museum in hot water over using "Canaan" instead of Palestine in labels, Ocean Vuong's photography, Lunar New Year celebrations in NYC, and Seph Rodney on the need for art that gives us an "elsewhere to imagine."

item.title: Inside Pratt SCPS: Where Practice Meets the Spotlight
item.description: Discover what happens when working creatives, career pivoters, and lifelong makers plug into art and design education at Pratt’s School of Continuing and Professional Studies.

item.title: Remembering Henrike Naumann, LaMonte McLemore, and Frederick Wiseman
item.description: This week, we honor Germany’s representative at the Venice Biennale, a singer and photographer, and a documentarian of the lives of institutions.

item.title: LA’s Art Scene Is Not a New York Outpost
item.description: Artist-run spaces represent the heart of Los Angeles’s art scene, yet most people still see the city’s identity as tied to the market — one that’s increasingly influenced by the East Coast.

item.title: The Museum at FIT Presents “Art X Fashion”
item.description: This exhibition explores the entangled and shifting relationship between fine art and fashion, tracing parallel aesthetics from 18th-century Rococo to postmodernism.

item.title: University of North Texas Students Withdraw Thesis Shows, Citing Censorship
item.description: It’s one of multiple actions in solidarity with artist Victor “Marka27” Quiñonez, whose exhibition of works critical of ICE violence was abruptly shuttered.

item.title: Representatives of Pride Flag’s Creator Sue Trump Administration
item.description: It’s one of two recent lawsuits targeting the government’s interventions across parks and monuments in the week after the Pride flag was removed from Stonewall.

item.title: The Self-Invention of Helene Schjerfbeck
item.description: The Finnish artist’s first major exhibition in the US is a moving and harrowing document of her growth, as well as the psychic and physical ravages of aging.

item.title: Brooklyn Navy Yard Evicts Drone Manufacturer After Months of Protests
item.description: Though listed as a “fine art and photography” business, Easy Aerial contracts with Customs and Border Protection and the Israeli military, activists long flagged.
